notes: Copy for the Sunday water check. *text* inside q/help/identity/shift renders in the script face. {name} and {town} are replaced. Every option on a branch carries tags that the recommendation reads; every opener option carries weights toward archetypes. Archetype ids come from archetypes.md.

scrutinizer.name: The Scrutinizer
scrutinizer.tag: You don’t take anyone’s word for it.
scrutinizer.identity: You’re on a well, and you know what that means: nobody is checking this water but you. You don’t take the inspector’s word, the neighbor’s word, or “it’s always been fine.” You want to see it.
scrutinizer.shift: Scrutinizers don’t guess. They *test.* Then they decide.
scrutinizer.resultHead: Scrutinizers test first. Here’s what the test is *for.*
scrutinizer.resultLead: Nobody tests a private well but the owner. The free test puts numbers on bacteria, arsenic, hardness and iron. You decide from there.

protector.name: The Protector
protector.tag: You check everything that touches your kid.
protector.identity: Car seat, crib, the paint, the food. You’ve checked it all. Water is the one thing in the house you can’t see, so it’s the one thing you haven’t.
protector.shift: Protectors don’t hope it’s fine. They *make sure.*
protector.resultLead: The water in the bottle is the one thing in the house you can’t check by looking. The test does, and the system handles what it finds.

fixer.name: The Fixer
fixer.tag: You don’t live with a problem you can solve.
fixer.identity: Spots on the glasses, the shower door, the water heater working too hard. You’ve scrubbed it, vinegared it, and you’re done managing it. You’d rather fix the cause.
fixer.shift: Fixers fix the *cause,* not the symptom.
fixer.resultLead: Scale, spots and dry skin are one problem with one cause: hard water. You fix it once, at the main line, for every faucet.

investigator.name: The Investigator
investigator.tag: You’ve read the report. You want the numbers.
investigator.identity: You pulled the utility report. You know what TTHM and PFAS are. What you don’t have is the number from your own kitchen tap, and you know a plant report isn’t that.
investigator.shift: Investigators don’t settle for the plant’s numbers. They get *their own.*
investigator.resultHead: Investigators get their own numbers. *Here’s the plan.*
investigator.resultLead: The utility reports on the plant. The test reports on your tap. Those are different numbers, and only one of them is yours.

freshstart.name: The Fresh Start
freshstart.tag: New house. Do it right from day one.
freshstart.identity: You just took the keys. You’re the kind of person who finds out what you inherited before it becomes a problem: the roof, the furnace, and the water.
freshstart.shift: Fresh Starts don’t inherit someone else’s shortcuts. They set *their own baseline.*
freshstart.resultHead: Fresh Starts set a baseline. *Here’s yours.*
freshstart.resultLead: One test, one written report, and you know exactly what this house’s water is on day one. Everything after that is a decision, not a guess.

standard.name: The Standard-Setter
standard.tag: You read the labels on your food.
standard.identity: You read labels. You notice when something’s off and you don’t pretend it isn’t. Whether it’s the taste or what you can’t taste, the tap hasn’t met your standard, and buying bottled is a workaround, not a fix.
standard.shift: Standard-Setters don’t work around it. They *raise the tap* to the standard.
standard.resultLead: Bottled water is a workaround with a weekly bill. The fix is at the tap, built for what you can and can’t taste, and it’s the last time you think about it.
